subject.title: feat(webchat): allow safe app-protocol links (obsidian://, things://, etc.)

question: Should assistant-rendered WebChat links be allowed to invoke local application protocols, and what action-level restrictions or user confirmation must protect that boundary?
rationale: Scheme names alone do not establish safe behavior: supported handlers include shortcut execution, note mutation, and extension-defined callbacks, so repository intent is required before choosing a permanent policy.

options.title: Default-block with explicit opt-in
options.body: Keep the current default and permit operator-selected schemes only through a centralized launcher that displays the destination and requests confirmation.

options.title: Narrow action-level allowlist
options.body: Allow only specifically reviewed scheme-and-action combinations with no write, automation, or extension-dispatch behavior.

options.title: Keep all app protocols blocked
options.body: Retain the current HTTP, HTTPS, and mailto boundary and decline clickable desktop-app links.

recommendation.title: Default-block with explicit opt-in
recommendation.body: Keep the current default and permit operator-selected schemes only through a centralized launcher that displays the destination and requests confirmation.

likelyOwner.reason: Their prior security work introduced the relevant markdown protocol boundary and provides the strongest available history signal.
